table: 0x0879B704 (522 u32 pointers to graph headers; the only code references are natives 0xB5..0xB9 and 0xD6..0xD8)
model: Each entry is an EVENT GRAPH, not a single script. Header = array of u32 step words, indexed by step number (step 0 = entry). A step word < 0x10000 is END: the graph finishes with that value (written to the runner's result halfword unless cancelled via 0x03002A58). Otherwise it points to a node blob {u16 next_step (LE, bytes 0-1), u8 kind (byte 2), u8 arg (byte 3), payload}. The step runner 0x080124F8 (thread struct 0x2C bytes from 0x0801246E: +0 header, +4 &result, +8 u16 current step, +0x14 params, +0x18 own params, +0x28 active node object) sets step = next_step, builds the node object via handler table 0x080728AC[kind], calls its start (vtable+4) and then polls vtable+8 every frame until done. VERIFIED: emulator trace of run_scene natives hits handler kind 5 for #37 and kind 0 for #516 from 0x08012563.
branching: Bytecode nodes (kind 0/4) override next_step with their return value: if the interpreter stack holds exactly one value at `end`, current step = that value (0x08011F90..0x08011F9A). Choice nodes (kind 3) store the selected option index in 0x03002A60 (read by native 0x18); the following bytecode node branches on it. VERIFIED by reading graph #28 (Z-Mart shop): choice -> native 0x18 == 0 -> return 4.
synchronous_runner: 0x08004098 (natives 0xD6..0xD8, item/equipment/loot callers) runs ONLY node 0, which must be kind 0 or 4 (byte 2 checked; anything else = assertion 0x0803DF14).

kinds.name: bytecode
kinds.payload: raw bytecode at blob+3 (byte 3 is the first opcode, not an arg)
kinds.consumer: 0x08011F5A: runs the interpreter 0x08004038 inside a world entity (vtable 0x08049E84) with the thread's params; natives may block (nested loops); return value -> next step

kinds.name: dialog_inline
kinds.payload: UTF-16 text inline at blob+4; arg = speaker portrait
kinds.note: no reachable node in the table

kinds.name: dialog_inline_format
kinds.payload: u32 pointer to a UTF-16 printf format at blob+4, bytecode at blob+8 computing the arguments (interpreter stack = argument list, %s takes a string POINTER, %d an int), formatted by 0x0803DB7C; arg = portrait
kinds.note: no reachable node in the table

kinds.name: choice
kinds.payload: UTF-16 text inline at blob+4: prompt, blank line, then "-Option" lines
kinds.consumer: 0x0801236E -> 0x08030C16 choice-box entity (vtable 0x0804A7C4, added to the world); selection index -> 0x03002A60
kinds.example:
graph #28 step 1: "Welcome to the Hercule City Z-Mart! How can I help you?

-Buy
-Sell

-End"

kinds.name: bytecode_lz
kinds.payload: Webfoot-LZ bitstream at blob+4 WITHOUT the 8-byte {type,size} container (byte 3 = 0); inflated by 0x08049120 into a 0x800-byte buffer. Decodes with engine/crates/wf-rom/src/lz.rs as if it were a type-1 container stream (initial literal width 1; stops at the end code) - VERIFIED equal to the game's output for graphs #2 #3 #6 #13 #450. NOTE: Rom::lz(blob+4) is wrong here (it would parse the first 8 stream bytes as a container header).

kinds.name: dialog
kinds.payload: u32 text ref at blob+4: bank = ref & 0x3F (container pointer table 0x087B5B64; 7 LZ banks), start = ((ref >> 6) & 0x7FFF) * 2 bytes, length = ref >> 21 UTF-16 units (no terminator in the bank); arg = speaker portrait id (0x08011F20: 0 or 7 = none, 1..6 = expression of the current character's form (form def +0x0F+id), >= 8 = portrait table 0x086F393C index)
kinds.example: graph #37: ref 0x04EECA00 -> "The game will not run on this hardware." (shown in the emulator)

kinds.name: dialog_format
kinds.payload: u32 text ref at blob+4 (as kind 5) = printf format; bytecode at blob+8 computes the arguments
kinds.example: graph #3 step 1: "%s has reached level %d!" with args (form_name native 0x16, get_level native 0xC8)

kinds.name: goto_graph
kinds.payload: u32 pointer to another graph header at blob+4
kinds.consumer: thread.header = that header, step = 0 (tail call); trivial node object vtable 0x0804AEB0

text_format: UTF-16LE; "\n" = line break; {xxxx} = control codes (see strtab.py); printf %s/%d in kinds 2/6.
